stem: Mark the range of $y = 2\cos\theta - 3$ on the $y$-number line: every $y$-value its graph reaches, from the lowest to the highest. Make an end filled if $y$ reaches that value and hollow if it only gets close.
solution: The cosine never goes below $-1$ and never above $1$, and it reaches both: $-1 \le \cos\theta \le 1$.
Multiply every part by $2$ (positive, so the inequality signs keep their direction): $-2 \le 2\cos\theta \le 2$.
Subtract $3$ from every part, because $q = -3$ lowers the whole graph: $-5 \le 2\cos\theta - 3 \le -1$.
So the range is $-5 \le y \le -1$. Mark $-5$ and $-1$ with filled circles, since $y$ reaches both values, and shade between them.
notes: Same instrument and mapping as the sine template, with cosine and a negative q so the shift runs downwards and the whole range sits below zero (the book's 3b is 2 cos(theta) - 4, so different numbers are used). Limits: range [-6,6], ends -5 and -1 are whole and inside it. Wrong intervals here: ignores-added-number gives [-2, 2] (mapped, likeliest); ends-are-the-equation-numbers gives [-3, 2]; sine-cosine-start-at-zero gives [-3, -1]; adds-q-to-one-end gives [-5, 2] or [-2, -1]. One predicate fires for all of them, so the three unmapped errors are named here, not diagnosed. endpoint-inclusion-wrong is unmapped for the same reason as in the sine template.
